test_title: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 08 Aug, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Find the value of sin (90 − x) cos (180 − (x − y)) + cos (90 − x) sin (180 − (y − x)).
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Put x = 90° and y = 0° in the given expression:

⇒ sin(90° − 90°) cos(180° − (90° − 0°)) + cos(90° − 90°) sin(180° − (0° − 90°))

⇒ sin(0°) cos(90°) + cos(0°) sin(270°)

⇒ 0 × 0 + 1 × (−1) = −1

Substituting y = 0° in the options, only Option 3 (−cos y) gives −1.

**∴ The correct answer is −cos y.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

sin(90° − x) cos(180° − (x − y)) + cos(90° − x) sin(180° − (y − x))

**Formula Used:**

sin(90° − θ) = cos θ

cos(90° − θ) = sin θ

cos(180° − θ) = −cos θ

sin(180° − θ) = sin θ

sin(−θ) = −sin θ

cos(A − B) = cos A cos B + sin A sin B

**Calculations:**

⇒ sin(90° − x) = cos x

⇒ cos(180° − (x − y)) = −cos(x − y)

⇒ cos(90° − x) = sin x

⇒ sin(180° − (y − x)) = sin(y − x) = −sin(x − y)

Substituting these values into the given expression:

⇒ (cos x) × (−cos(x − y)) + (sin x) × (−sin(x − y))

⇒ −cos x cos(x − y) − sin x sin(x − y)

⇒ −[cos x cos(x − y) + sin x sin(x − y)]

Using the identity cos(A − B) = cos A cos B + sin A sin B:

⇒ −[cos(x − (x − y))]

⇒ −cos(x − x + y)

⇒ −cos y

**∴ The correct answer is −cos y.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Signs by Quadrant (ASTC Rule)

1st Quadrant: All positive | 2nd Quadrant: Sine & Cosec positive | 3rd Quadrant: Tan & Cot positive | 4th Quadrant: Cos & Sec positive.

Compound Angle Identities

sin(A + B) = sin A cos B + cos A sin B 
 cos(A + B) = cos A cos B − sin A sin B

Complementary & Supplementary Angles

Angles that sum to 90° are complementary (sin(90°−θ) = cos θ). Angles summing to 180° are supplementary (cos(180°−θ) = −cos θ).
